<!-- updated: 2026-10-19 / uoink v3.10.0 -->
# Uoink 3.10.0: CLI, skill, and agent setup

> A local library for the videos and podcasts you study, that any AI you use can search and cite.

Free, MIT-licensed. No account or Uoink-hosted corpus. Model dependencies can send telemetry. Made by Ryan Biddy (@replayryan), a personal side project.

Uoink 3.10.0 adds the uoink command for local agents, a portable Uoink skill, the Claude Code plugin marketplace at ryanbiddy/uoink-agent-kit, and setup recipes for 38 clients and integrations. Start with `uoink status` in a new terminal after installation.

Uoink is listed in the official MCP registry as io.github.ryanbiddy/uoink. Both MCP transports advertise flattened tool schemas; the server still checks the exact schema for every call.

Every Uoink tool is available through the standard connection used by Claude Desktop (.mcpb), Claude Code, and Cursor: 91 tools over stdio and 91 in the HTTP registry. Agents can capture pages, X posts, Reddit threads, notes, and images; use writing, script, and workspace tools; and work with sources and the Library queue. UOINK_MCP_TOOLSET=core keeps the previous 35-tool set for clients that cap tool counts. Full mode keeps those tools first. Consent gates are unchanged. No data or settings changes besides the optional PATH entry. No new index or migration. Installing over the previous release keeps your library and saved captures.

## Install

Windows 10/11 today. A Mac version is in development. Unsigned installer, about 390 MB; no admin rights needed. If Windows SmartScreen shows a warning, choose More info, then Run anyway. Installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink. Sideload the browser extension from the install; Chrome Web Store listing pending. Chrome (tested); other Chromium browsers such as Edge and Brave may work but are not tested. Open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select %LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink\extension. Click the puzzle-piece Extensions icon in the toolbar and pin Uoink so the Uoink button stays visible.

After updating, reload the extension once. If its ID changes to the pinned bkcapfidedhfcjpmjabeopfbcjcbmdmi, reapply extension preferences. Saved captures are unaffected.

- [Install](https://uoink.app/install): helper and extension instructions.
- [Latest release](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/latest): installer and Claude Desktop .mcpb bundle.
- [Windows installer](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.10.0/Uoink-Setup-3.10.0.exe): Uoink 3.10.0.
- [3.10.0 release notes](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/tag/v3.10.0): CLI, skill, plugin marketplace, and agent setup.

## Capture and library

YouTube: timestamped transcript, screenshots, top comments, channel context, metadata. Also X video and post text, podcast RSS/Atom feeds, web articles, and Reddit threads. Capture with the YouTube button, right-click, Alt+U, or your AI agent. Files are structured Markdown plus a JSON sidecar on your own disk, indexed in one local library.

3.9.0 introduced the previously unpublished Living Library work: clip search and evidence cards; standing capture for YouTube channels, YouTube playlists, and podcast RSS; MCP library search, item reads, resource templates and prompts; cited range export with speaker labels, chapters and provenance; and chapter navigation where chapters exist. Podcast transcripts enter the searchable corpus and interrupted jobs resume after restart. Feed audio stays off until Auto-ingest is enabled. Captures show toast notifications that can be muted and are suppressed during fullscreen use. Entity extraction is opt-in and off by default; the usage meter shows real Anthropic usage; the recall hook is hardened against prompt injection.

The redesigned dashboard has Library search-or-paste, Reader, Activity with a five-step capture strip, and one Settings page that saves individual preferences automatically. The extension popup and setup provide capture and connection controls. Caption rate limits no longer fail an entire YouTube capture: local transcription can use an already-downloaded model, or the missing transcript stays labeled. Requests are paced and yt-dlp is newer. Waiting, failures and cancellation remain distinct; cancellation is refused once publication starts.

Five local research playbooks cover outlier posts, transcript intelligence, comment mining, creator teardowns and repurposing over the user's own library. MCP agents can request cited packets without model or network calls. Optional ScrapeCreators discovery is off by default, uses the user's own key, and defaults to a 25-credit daily cap. Paid calls require credit confirmation and a dashboard intent or separately enabled agent discovery.

Security changes pin the extension ID and check it when minting tokens, reject scripted clicks on capture buttons, add private-network protection to supported fetch paths, scrub paths and credentials from returned and stored job errors, and confine corpus imports to the output folder's _exports directory. Requests inside yt-dlp and the browser renderer are outside the private-network checks; the local diagnostic log can retain raw tool output.

The library does not organize, file, or re-shelve itself. The Librarian only proposes; applying is off by default and its quality gate has not passed.

- [Features](https://uoink.app/features): feature details.
- [Sources](https://uoink.app/sources): capture paths.
- [How it works](https://uoink.app/how-it-works): capture to cited corpus.

## AI access

Clipboard paste with transcript and frames works with ChatGPT and claude.ai. Uoink does not connect to the ChatGPT app over MCP. Local MCP exposes 91 tools over stdio and 91 in the HTTP registry, counted from the release source. Previously tested MCP clients include Claude Desktop and Cursor. The 3.10.0 testing notes below cover Claude Code, Codex CLI, the CLI and skill, and the plugin's limits. OpenAPI 3.1 bridges local agents that do not speak MCP.

- [Developers](https://uoink.app/developers): MCP clients, portable skill, plugin marketplace, CLI, and testing notes.
- [MCP](https://uoink.app/mcp): transport details and tools.
- [MCP manifest](https://uoink.app/mcp/manifest.json): all 91 tools, schemas and stdio availability.
- [Feature manifest](https://uoink.app/api/features-manifest): feature URLs and summaries.
- [Full text](https://uoink.app/llms-full.txt): setup details.

## Network calls and retention

Capture contacts source sites and can use FxTwitter for X text even when a post was not identified as truncated. Enabled subscriptions poll with automatic capture off, and connected agents can register them. Turning automatic capture off stops new starts; already-started work may finish. Stop Uoink stops polling until restart; Autostart on login controls the next Windows login. The authenticated local API can archive subscriptions; legacy feed and monitored-playlist enable controls cover only sources with those records.

X text capture defaults to true. Setting x_text_capture_enabled to false in local settings stops both syndication and FxTwitter text requests. There is no dashboard or extension toggle, and POST /settings does not accept this field. Video capture is separate.

Removing the saved Anthropic key attempts to delete the current credential, but a legacy Yoink credential or older plaintext settings entry can remain, and deletion failures can go unreported. Check Windows Credential Manager and the active profile settings; local removal does not revoke the key at Anthropic. Disconnect agents in their clients to end access.

Extension setup and previews can load remote thumbnails. After copying a completed capture, the extension opens claude.ai/new without pasting or submitting the content, even with AI off; there is no setting to disable the tab. Missing Whisper-model downloads require a per-request approval flag that a connected agent can set without a Uoink prompt. Optional speaker labeling downloads pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 from Hugging Face when needed and can send your Hugging Face token to huggingface.co. Supporting transcription and alignment models can also download from Hugging Face or PyTorch hosts, and language data from NLTK. The pinned pyannote-audio 4.0.7 dependency enables metrics by default, including during voice-activity detection with speaker labeling off. Uoink provides no dashboard switch; PYANNOTE_METRICS_ENABLED=false in the helper environment disables those metrics. Release checks query GitHub when the cache needs refreshing or a caller forces a check, without sending the library or installing an update.

Captures, local indexes and settings remain on disk. Logs can contain source URLs and paths. Exported files and optional mirrors create additional copies; sync software can upload them. The extension screenshot interval uses browser sync storage. Trash cleanup is attempted at startup and daily for items older than 30 days. Uninstall retains library data and credentials but removes edited topics.json routing rules. The website separately uses Vercel Web Analytics. See https://uoink.app/privacy for controls and retention details.

Connected agents can start paid Anthropic calls with the saved key when the user allows those actions, even with automatic analysis off. Relevant library text and, for research, saved discovery rows can be sent. Local MCP playbook packets make no model call.

ScrapeCreators receives the typed handle, channel ID or query only after discovery is enabled and the request authorized. Local run files store that input, request identity, normalized candidates and metrics, credit accounting, coverage, queue state and errors, including failed runs. No raw vendor responses, thumbnails or API keys are stored in these files. The daily purge removes run files older than 90 days; local playbooks may reuse eligible snapshots up to 30 days old.

## Set it up with an agent (Windows 10/11)
Windows 10/11 today. A Mac version is in development. Uoink v3.10.0 is free and MIT-licensed; the unsigned installer is about 390 MB. No admin rights needed.
[Agent installation steps](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/blob/main/llms-install.md): download, verify SHA-256, install, and connect.
### An agent can run
1. Download [Uoink-Setup-3.10.0.exe](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.10.0/Uoink-Setup-3.10.0.exe) to `$env:TEMP\Uoink-Setup-3.10.0.exe`.
2. Before running it, compare `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "$env:TEMP\Uoink-Setup-3.10.0.exe"` with the installer entry in [SHA256SUMS.txt](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.10.0/SHA256SUMS.txt).
3. Install per user: `Start-Process -Wait -FilePath "$env:TEMP\Uoink-Setup-3.10.0.exe" -ArgumentList '/VERYSILENT','/SUPPRESSMSGBOXES','/NORESTART'`. It installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink` with Add the uoink command to PATH for AI agents checked by default. No data or settings changes besides the optional PATH entry; no new index or migration. Installing over the previous release keeps the library and saved captures.
4. Open a new terminal, run `uoink status`, then connect a client below. Silent install does not start Uoink; MCP works without it running. For the dashboard, browser button, and monitored-playlist polling, start "Uoink" from the Start menu or run `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\python\pythonw.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\server.py"` in PowerShell.
### The person must do
- Allow the unsigned installer if Windows asks. For SmartScreen, choose More info, then Run anyway.
- For the optional browser button: open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select %LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink\extension. An agent can capture without the button.
Chrome (tested); other Chromium browsers such as Edge and Brave may work but are not tested.
Click the puzzle-piece Extensions icon in the toolbar and pin Uoink so the Uoink button stays visible.
- After updating, reload the extension once. If its ID changes to bkcapfidedhfcjpmjabeopfbcjcbmdmi, reapply extension preferences; saved captures are unaffected.

## Connect your AI
Official MCP registry: io.github.ryanbiddy/uoink
- Setup recipes: `uoink connect --list` prints setup choices for 38 clients and integrations. Run `uoink connect <client>` for config or instructions and their destination; it does not edit client settings. Run the printed Claude Code command in PowerShell; merge other clients' entries into the location shown, then restart their MCP connection.
- Codex: `uoink connect codex` prints tables for `~/.codex/config.toml`. VS Code: `uoink connect vscode` prints config for `.vscode/mcp.json`. The dashboard's Add to Cursor / Add to VS Code buttons open the client's review flow; acceptance of these buttons is not yet tested.
- Uoink skill for Claude Code, Codex, pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw: `uoink skill path` locates it; `uoink skill install --to <dir>` copies it with references into a uoink subfolder of the parent skills directory. Restart the agent or reload its skills.
- Claude Code plugin for a default install: `claude plugin marketplace add ryanbiddy/uoink-agent-kit`, then `claude plugin install uoink@uoink`. Restart Claude Code and enable the plugin MCP server when prompted. Custom installs use `uoink connect claude-code` plus the standalone skill; avoid duplicate MCP entries.
- CLI examples: `uoink search "working memory" --limit 5`, `uoink recent --limit 10`, `uoink note "A useful thought" --title "Research note"`. Agents can search sources, read evidence, capture URLs, save notes, and call registry tools. Local reads work without the helper running; capture and paid tools keep their existing gates. The agent must be able to execute Uoink on the Windows machine holding the library.
Tested on a clean, isolated install: Claude Code 2.1.302 over MCP (all 91 tools listed; a note saved and listed back); Claude Code with the skill and CLI only (skill loaded; uoink note and uoink recent ran); Codex CLI 0.153.4 over MCP (a note saved and listed back); CLI status, note, recent, and connect. The Claude Code plugin loads its skill and starts its MCP server; its tool calls were not run end to end because the test install is isolated from a normal one. Not yet tested: Gemini CLI and pi (no sign-in on the test machine) and every other uoink connect recipe. Claude Desktop and Cursor retain their earlier MCP testing status.

Claude Desktop: download and open [uoink-3.10.0.mcpb](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.10.0/uoink-3.10.0.mcpb). Desktop installs it as an extension and asks for your Uoink folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink). Enter the full path; Desktop does not expand %LOCALAPPDATA%. After updating, reinstall the bundle and restart Desktop.

Claude Code (verified with 2.1.302, including all tools listed, a note saved, and recent captures read): run this in PowerShell with absolute paths:

```powershell
claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio uoink -e PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 -e PYTHONUTF8=1 -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\python\python.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\uoink_mcp.py"
```

Cursor and other stdio clients use this config. Replace %LOCALAPPDATA% in both paths with your full app-data directory, or copy the generated config from the extension's Settings page. Restart the client after saving.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "uoink": {
      "command": "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Uoink\\python\\python.exe",
      "args": [
        "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Uoink\\uoink_mcp.py"
      ],
      "env": {
        "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8",
        "PYTHONUTF8": "1"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor is reported to send only the first 40 tools to its agent. Add `"UOINK_MCP_TOOLSET": "core"` to the server env to keep the previous 35-tool set and stay under that cap. Omit it for the full toolset, which is the default. ChatGPT and claude.ai use copy and paste only; Uoink does not connect to the ChatGPT app over MCP.

## Skill directories

Run `uoink skill install --to <dir>` with your agent's parent skills directory. In PowerShell:
- Claude Code: `uoink skill install --to "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills"`.
- Codex: `uoink skill install --to "$env:USERPROFILE\.agents\skills"` (older setups may use `~/.codex/skills`).
- pi: `uoink skill install --to "$env:USERPROFILE\.pi\agent\skills"`.
- Hermes Agent: `uoink skill install --to "$env:USERPROFILE\.hermes\skills"`.
- OpenClaw: `uoink skill install --to "$env:USERPROFILE\.openclaw\skills"`.

The copy includes references. An existing copy needs `--force` to overwrite. Restart the agent or reload its skills. A skill copied into a remote environment does not expose this PC's library.

## Local HTTP and OpenAPI

HTTP JSON-RPC: http://127.0.0.1:5179/mcp/v1. Include X-Uoink-Token, read from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink\token.txt.
OpenAPI 3.1 spec: http://127.0.0.1:5179/openapi/v1/spec.json.

## Podcast standing capture

Watch RSS/Atom feeds. Per-feed auto-ingest is optional: when enabled, new episodes download as local MP3s and transcribe locally with WhisperX.

## Tool inventory

Source: v3.10.0, commit 93ab34151715a423dc4950f5c5b3b56563d3c737. The shared TOOL_REGISTRY and default stdio inventory expose 91 tools over stdio and 91 in the HTTP registry, checked against .mcpb/manifest.json. Tool names, descriptions, HTTP registry schemas, and transport labels are in https://uoink.app/mcp/manifest.json. Both HTTP and stdio advertise the same flattened top-level schema variants for client compatibility; handlers still validate the exact registry schema.
